meta.attribution: Text from the Unofficial Elder Scrolls Pages (UESP), https://en.uesp.net/ ; each record names its page and revision id.
method: Tokens: the dovahzul field of every corpus record, lower-cased, cut into runs of letters; an apostrophe inside a word stays, a hyphen separates tokens. Dialogue records contribute only their dragon-language segments.
Headwords: every spelling in entries[].word_forms of the lexicon, lower-cased; 'Kel(le)' counts as kel and kelle; 'Vo...' counts as vo.

explained_by_documented_rules: tokens that are not headwords but follow a pattern stated in the Grammar section of Lore:Dragon Language (plural, possessive, our, perfect) or are two to four headwords written together (compound). A compound reading is mechanical and can be a coincidence, above all when it uses two-letter headwords; such parts are listed under short_parts.

oov: every other token, with one class each. Names stay in oov even when a compound reading exists. possible_compound_readings lists up to five ways to cut the token into headwords (best first: fewest two-letter parts, then fewest parts); these are mechanical and the wiki's own analysis, where it has one, is in basis.
A compound made only of two-letter headwords is not accepted as an explanation (tu + um for 'tuum'): such tokens stay in oov.
count = occurrences over all records; count_in_unique_texts leaves out records marked duplicate_of. texts = ids of all records the token occurs in.

classes.name: A proper name: a dragon, dragon priest or place name listed in the Names section of the dictionary page, a name the corpus records with a wiki-stated meaning, or a word that the wiki's English translation of the same text carries over unchanged (people and places named on word walls).
classes.spelling variant or error: Differs from a headword, or from another corpus token that is explained, by one letter, one swapped pair, a dropped apostrophe or a doubled letter; or the wiki itself marks it {{sic}}. Usually a typo in the game text or on the wiki, or another official spelling.
classes.inflected or derived form (pattern not i: A headword plus an ending that the dictionary page's Grammar section does not describe but that the corpus attests, e.g. the possessive -ii (Thu'umii 'his Voice').
classes.likely lexicon omission (meaning stated: Not a headword and not derivable from one, but a wiki page states a meaning for it: a hover gloss on a one-word segment, a word-by-word shout meaning, a phrase entry on the dictionary page, or a sentence on a name page.
classes.word of another language inside dragon t: English (or other) wording that stands inside an official dragon-language text.
classes.unclassified: No test decides it. Either a lexicon omission whose meaning the wiki only gives inside a longer translation, or an error.

meta.class_order: manual reading; marked {{sic}} by the wiki; name (dictionary Names/Locations, corpus name record, or carried into the English of the same text); headword without apostrophe; one letter from a headword with the same stated meaning; headword + an ending of one letter, or of two or three letters when no headword is one letter away; one letter from a rule-explained token; one letter from a headword and no stated meaning; meaning stated on the wiki; unclassified

di.evidence: Skyrim:Alduin prints 'Di kiirre fen alok.' with the hover gloss 'My children will rise.'; the headword for 'my' is Dii.

dovah's.class: word of another language inside dragon text
dovah's.evidence: English possessive 's on the headword Dovah, in the official ESO style name "Dovah's Du'ul" (Online:Dovah's Du'ul Style).

kfir.evidence: Blades:Shulkunaak writes 'Kfir voth ahkrin'; Blades:Facing the Dragon gives the same line as 'Krif voth ahkrin' (Krif 'Fight' is a headword).

men.evidence: Skyrim:Anniversary Edition quotes the cover text 'Naal Thuum Zeim Men Eruvos' with the wiki's reading '(by shout through many years)'; 'men' stands where 'many' stands in that reading, but the page states no word-by-word meaning. The headword for 'many' on the dictionary page is Pogaan.

mere.evidence: Skyrim:Paarthurnax (dragon): 'Ni liivrah hin mere. True, this is not the final krongah - victory.' The wiki glosses no word of the sentence; Liiv 'Wither' and Hin 'Your' are headwords, 'mere' is not.

moron.evidence: Lore:Dragon Language: Myth no More, passage 1, prints 'moron au' where the wall itself (Skyrim:Aura Whisper, wall 2) reads MORO NAU ('glory on'): a word-division slip in the book text as the wiki gives it. The 'au' that follows it counts as the headword Au in this file.

ri.evidence: SkyrimVSE:Combat spells the Soul Tear shout 'Ri Vaaz Zoll'; the Skyrim shout page has Rii Vaaz Zol.

tuum.evidence: Skyrim:High Hrothgar gives the banner text 'THUUM TUUM' and says the banners cannot be translated completely. Tu 'Hammer' + Um 'Twin' is a possible cut but nothing on the wiki supports it.

zil.evidence: Skyrim:Alduin prints 'zil gro dovah ulse!' in one place and 'ziil gro dovah ulse!' in another; Ziil is the headword.

zoll.evidence: SkyrimVSE:Combat spells the Soul Tear shout 'Ri Vaaz Zoll'; the Skyrim shout page has Rii Vaaz Zol.

meta.headwords_not_in_corpus_note: headwords_not_in_corpus lists the lexicon spellings that never occur as a token of their own in the corpus. Some occur only inside a longer token (ahmul in ahmulii, hadrim in hadrimme); the rest are attested only by the source the dictionary page cites for them.
caveats: Classes are best readings made by fixed tests plus a short manual list; they are not rulings on the language. 'name' in particular is decided by the English text of the same record and can be wrong for a word the translator chose to leave untranslated.
A token counted as a headword can still be a different word that happens to be spelled the same (the lexicon lists several homographs).
The corpus keeps the wiki's spelling, so wiki typos appear as tokens.
